To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
memory-centric networks with HMCs can efficiently utilize processor channels for different traffic patterns, provide higher bandwidth and lower latency, and lead to higher performance.
memory-centric networks with HMCs can efficiently utilize processor-to-processor and processor-to-memory bandwidth, and achieve lower latency and higher performance than processor-centric networks.

memory-centric networks are more efficient than processor-centric networks in utilizing processor bandwidth for different communication patterns, that the distributor-based network is a good network design for memory-centric systems, and that a pass-through microarchitectural approach, which includes a proper intra-HMC design, is necessary for efficient utilization of memory bandwidth in memory-centric systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
memory-centric network architectures and their microarchitectural implications.
the design of memory-centric interconnects with HMCs, which are expected to become the mainstream DRAM technology in the near future.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
memory-centric network architectures can achieve better performance and energy efficiency for different applications and workloads.

memory-centric system interconnects are more efficient than processor-centric interconnects in the presence of Hybrid Memory Cubes, and that a pass-through micro-architecture with adaptive routing is a promising approach to exploit the benefits of memory-centric networks.
the proposed memory-centric interconnect design is a good solution to the memory bottleneck.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
memory-centric network architectures are a good choice for future systems with HMCs, as they can provide better performance and scalability.
memory-centric network architecture can be a promising solution for future systems with high bandwidth requirements.
memory-centric networks with Hybrid Memory Cube are promising to improve memory bandwidth, latency, and energy efficiency for future systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
memory-centric system interconnect designs are a viable alternative to processor-centric ones.
the system interconnect should be designed around memory bandwidth, not processor bandwidth, to achieve higher performance and energy efficiency.
memory-centric networks are a promising approach for future system interconnects.
